children: Shares of Vistance Networks fell after the company reported lower revenue in the recent quarter and said its top executive is stepping down.
The stock declined 16%, to $5.41, on Thursday, having lost more than 70% of its value year to date.

The provider of connectivity and cable solutions before the bell swung to a third-quarter profit from continuing operations of $54.7 million, or 24 cents a share, from a loss of $18.9 million, or 16 cents a share, a year earlier.
Stripping out certain one-time items, adjusted earnings came in at 23 cents a share.

"While memory chip pressures and customer deployment timing continue to impact near-term performance, we remain confident in the long-term demand for our products and opportunities to expand our portfolio," Chief Executive Chuck Treadway said.
Separately, Treadway on Thursday said Treadway will step down from the roles of president and CEO, effective Feb. 1, 2027.
